market_view: The Iran war still dominates: Brent is near $114 (+11% in 20 days) and Dutch gas is up 38%, with fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi refining and mine damage near Hormuz offset by Qatari mediation. Europe is pricing tentative Russia-Ukraine de-escalation (a widening local truce in Kherson, possible US sanctions relief). Trade frictions are broadening (Canadian autos, US-EU over Airbus), and the Fed meets this week ahead of the 3 November US midterms, with markets braced for a hawkish hold.

events.title: Houthi missile strike on Saudi Ras Tanura refinery; Saudi supply at three-decade low
events.summary: Yemen's Houthis say they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, its largest; Saudi forces report intercepting further missiles. The IEA says Saudi oil supply has fallen to a more than three-decade low after the attacks.

impacts.rationale: Attack on the largest Saudi refinery plus IEA-reported supply low -> tighter crude and product balance -> producers up, airlines and cruise lines down. Brent already +11% in 20 days, so size kept moderate.

events.title: Tanker hits mines near Hormuz; Iran asserts control of the strait
events.summary: Iran's army says an oil tanker caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's leadership stressed control over the strait and threatened legal action against a South Korean shipowner; CENTCOM denied Iranian claims that US forces had left.

impacts.rationale: Mines and Iranian threats against named shipowners -> higher war-risk insurance and freight rates through Hormuz -> tanker and shipping owners gain.
Physical damage to shipping keeps the regional war premium in oil, defence and gold, and weighs on airlines.

events.title: Qatar presents Iran with a deal to end the war; US warns of renewed strikes after midterms
events.summary: Qatari mediators presented Iran with a new proposal to end the war, and Iran welcomed regional security talks; Qatar says any mediation requires reopening Hormuz. Separately, the US warned Gulf states of a possible short, intense renewal of the war after the midterms.

impacts.rationale: A credible peace framework would cut the oil and war premium; offset by the US warning of a renewed campaign after 3 November, so confidence is low.

events.title: Qatar extends LNG force majeure to Italy's Edison until year-end
events.summary: QatarEnergy extended force majeure on LNG cargoes to Italy's Edison until the end of December, keeping European winter supply tight. EU farmers are cutting fertilizer demand because of high prices.

impacts.rationale: Less Qatari LNG into Italy through winter -> TTF stays high -> margin pressure on European chemicals, support for US gas producers. TTF already +38% in 20 days, so mostly priced.

events.title: Russia-Ukraine: local Kherson truce widens; US weighs easing sanctions on Russia's investment fund
events.summary: A US-brokered local ceasefire in Oleshky was extended across the Kherson region with no breaches reported. Norway's and Finland's leaders held a rare call with Putin. The NYT reports the US is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund.

impacts.rationale: A widening truce and signs of US sanctions relief raise the odds of a broader deal -> reconstruction materials and Polish assets gain. The truce is local and Putin's rhetoric stays hard, so the size is small.
Peace headlines have repeatedly knocked European defence stocks short term, even though budgets are structural; low confidence.

events.title: US trade official warns EU loan to Airbus threatens the US-EU trade truce
events.summary: A Trump trade official warned that an EU loan to Airbus threatens the trade truce between the US and the EU.

impacts.rationale: A state-aid dispute could unravel the truce -> risk of new US tariffs on EU autos, luxury and spirits.
Airbus is the direct target of any US retaliation over the loan (the old Airbus-Boeing subsidy fight).

events.title: Threat of 50% US tariffs on Canadian-built cars amid tense trade talks
events.summary: Honda warned that 50% US tariffs on Canadian auto imports would be catastrophic for the industry. Trump praised Canadian separatists during delicate trade talks.

impacts.rationale: Stellantis assembles vehicles in Ontario (Windsor, Brampton) for the US market -> direct tariff cost.
GM builds trucks in Ontario for the US -> higher costs if tariffs rise.
Ford's Canadian plants (Oakville, Windsor engines) feed US production -> moderate exposure.

events.title: US Section 232 tariffs on imported wind turbines and components
events.summary: A presidential proclamation adjusting imports of wind turbines and their parts was published in the Federal Register. It was signed on 22 October, so markets have known for several days.

impacts.rationale: Siemens Gamesa ships turbines and parts into the US -> tariffs hurt US orders and margins; partly priced (-12% in 20 days).
GE Vernova's US-built onshore turbines gain share against tariffed imports.

events.title: Defense Production Act determination for US petroleum production, refining and logistics
events.summary: A presidential determination under Section 303 of the Defense Production Act covers domestic petroleum production, refining and logistics capacity. It was signed on 22 October.

impacts.rationale: Opens DPA funding and priority support for US oil output, refining and pipelines -> modest support for midstream and producers, negative read for solar.

events.title: Fed decision this week with a hawkish tilt expected
events.summary: The Fed is expected to hold rates this week, but Chair Warsh may point to further hikes; Treasury yields rose ahead of the decision.

impacts.rationale: Guidance toward more hikes -> higher yields -> banks gain, homebuilders and REITs lose. Homebuilders rallied 5-7% this week, adding downside if the Fed is hawkish.

events.title: Belgium prepares forced nationalisation of Engie's nuclear plants
events.summary: Belgium is preparing a forced nationalisation of its nuclear plants after talks with operator Engie stalled.

impacts.rationale: A forced takeover risks compensation below book value and a legal fight; partly offset if it removes Engie's nuclear liabilities.

events.title: Israeli election ends without a clear winner
events.summary: Israel's election, with turnout of 77.7%, produced no clear winner. Netanyahu's bloc leads the count, and Arab parties may hold the balance between Netanyahu and Eisenkot.

impacts.rationale: Deadlock -> weeks of coalition talks or a repeat election -> policy uncertainty for Israeli assets after a +2.8% run into the vote.

events.title: EU and Australia fund non-Chinese critical minerals supply
events.summary: The EU plans a large investment in Australia's critical minerals to reduce dependence on China. Australia will fund a rare earths project with A$180 million.

impacts.rationale: Government funding and offtake for non-Chinese supply -> continued policy support for rare earth and battery-metal producers.
